newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain reveals plan to ensure fiscal stability.
newsitem.headline: Spain reveals plan to ensure fiscal stability.

text.p: Spain revealed a plan to ensure fiscal stability into the next century, pledging to reduce the public deficit to 1.6 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2000 from a planned 3.0 percent in 1997.
In a statement, Spain also said it expected average growth of 3.2 percent between 1997 and 2000.

"The outlook for the economic cycle suggests average growth of 3.2 percent between 1997 and the year 2000 and average inflation in terms of the private consumption deflator of 2.3 percent," the government said in a statement.
It also said it expected public debt to fall to 65.3 percent of gross domestic product in 2000 from 68.2 percent of GDP in 1997.

"Given this economic outlook, the budget projection reflects a continual fall in the deficit of public administrations in terms of GDP from three percent in 1997 to 1.6 percent in 2000. Even in the most unfavourable situation in terms of expected growth, the public deficit would be systematically below three percent of GDP," the statement said.
Fiscal consolidation will be focused on restraining current expenditures, whose portion of GDP will be reduced by two percentage points during the reference period.
